title: Is the flat per-iteration align cost in progressive seeding a flat alignment count?
body:
In progressive seeding, nail runs `mmseqs align` once per iteration on a slice of the prefilter db. `n_take` doubles each iteration, and the active set of queries shrinks. On the mgy run the 12 iterations cost 2.5 to 4.0 s each, with no trend. The measurements in the notes rule out a fixed cost per call. A call with nothing to align costs 45 ms against 2,455,940 targets.

## Proposal

Capture the alignment count of each iteration on the 48-thread box. The working reading is that the count stays near constant. `n_take` doubles while the active set roughly halves. The queries that survive align deeper candidates, and those are real hits that cost 2 to 3 times as much as a quick reject.

If the counts are flat, this issue closes with that fact. If the counts fall while the time stays flat, the cost is inside `mmseqs align`, and the next step is to look at its work per query record.

## Rejected

- Fewer iterations, through a larger `--prog-n` or a faster growth factor. All 12 calls together carry at most 0.5 s of fixed cost out of 36 s.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/2aff5e6c
notes.text: First measurement, at 4 threads on the 16-core box. The mmseqs binary there turned out to be an aarch64 build running under `qemu-aarch64-static`, so these numbers are 5 to 8 times too slow, and note 8b9ec3b1 supersedes them with a native rerun. The ratios and the conclusion held. Wall time tracks the alignment count, and a call with nothing to align is cheap.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/2aff5e6c
notes.text:
Rerun with a native x86-64 mmseqs, version `8cc5ce3`, at 4 threads on the 16-core box.

| prefilter db | targets | alignments | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty | 100,000 | 0 | 3 to 4 ms |
| empty | 2,455,940 | 0 | 45 ms |
| empty, at 1 thread | 2,455,940 | 0 | 64 ms |
| 20,795 empty records | 100,000 | 0 | 8 ms |
| 20,795 random pairs | 100,000 | 20,795 | 63 ms |
| iteration slice 0 | 100,000 | 4,149,229 | 9.28 s |
| iteration slice 1 | 100,000 | 3,647,173 | 6.35 s |
| iteration slice 2 | 100,000 | 515,289 | 1.03 s |
| iteration slice 3 | 100,000 | 249,239 | 0.56 s |
| iteration slice 4 | 100,000 | 81,410 | 0.24 s |
| iteration slice 5 | 100,000 | 21,552 | 0.14 s |

The iteration slices come from the leftover 100k-target run in `nail-benchmarks/data/tmp-nail`. The fixed cost grows with the number of targets, at about 18 ns per target record. That fits mmseqs reading the 45 MB target index on every call, though nobody has profiled it. Wall time tracks the alignment count at about 2.2 µs per alignment. On the mgy run the 12 calls cost at most 12 × 45 ms, which is 0.5 s of the 36 s align total. The iteration count is not the lever.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/2aff5e6c
notes.text:
How to get the counts on the 48-thread box with no code change. Run nail with its tmp dir kept, so `prog-seed/<N>/pdb` survives for each iteration. Then replay each slice with `time-align.sh`, which prints the wall time and the "alignments calculated" count that mmseqs reports:

```bash
time-align.sh <label> <qdb> <tdb> <pdb> <outdir> <evalue> [threads]
```

`<evalue>` is the seed p-value threshold times the target count, as `run_mmseqs_align` computes it. The script lives in `tmp-claude/2026-10-08-align-fixed-cost` on the 16-core box and needs copying over. nail itself captures mmseqs's stdout in `run()` in `util.rs` and prints it only on failure, so a normal run loses the count.

notes.author: jackroddy/4125deb5
notes.text:
Measured on the 48-thread box, `catalyst`, at `bb3c392`. nail and mmseqs ran on the 48 physical cores of NUMA node 0, through `numactl --membind=0 --physcpubind=0,2,...,94`, at `-t 48`. The flags were the ones `stage-times` passes: `-E 10 --mmseqs-s 12.0 --seed-mode prog -s`. The inputs were the `mgy` part of the `stage-times` set, 20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 MGnify targets, with native mmseqs `8cc5ce3`. The run took 421.7 s, and progressive seeding ran 12 align iterations for 34.4 s.

I replayed each `prog-seed/<N>/pdb` through `mmseqs align` with the run's arguments, under `/usr/bin/time`. Each replay came within 0.06 s of its iteration in the run's own tree. Iteration numbers below count from 0, and the tree counts them from 1.

| iteration | alignments | queries with pairs | largest query slice | wall, s | cpu |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4,155,995 | 20,781 | 200 | 2.34 | 4146% |
| 1 | 7,901,642 | 19,755 | 400 | 2.92 | 4167% |
| 2 | 6,995,146 | 8,745 | 800 | 2.58 | 3911% |
| 3 | 7,600,000 | 4,750 | 1,600 | 2.53 | 3927% |
| 4 | 8,087,852 | 2,528 | 3,200 | 2.58 | 3868% |
| 5 | 8,633,600 | 1,349 | 6,400 | 2.37 | 4224% |
| 6 | 8,896,000 | 695 | 12,800 | 2.49 | 4065% |
| 7 | 8,550,400 | 334 | 25,600 | 2.64 | 3685% |
| 8 | 6,809,600 | 133 | 51,200 | 3.02 | 2729% |
| 9 | 4,198,400 | 41 | 102,400 | 3.86 | 1500% |
| 10 | 819,200 | 4 | 204,800 | 3.04 | 421% |
| 11 | 401,544 | 1 | 401,544 | 3.92 | 150% |

The counts are not flat. They rise from 4.2M to 8.9M by iteration 6 and fall to 0.4M by iteration 11. Through iteration 7 the working reading holds. The count stays between 7M and 9M, and 37 to 42 cores are busy.

From iteration 8 on, the largest query slice sets the wall time. Iteration 11 aligns 401,544 pairs for one query at 150% cpu. Iterations 8 to 11 take 13.8 s of the 34.4 s. The cpu figures fit `mmseqs align` giving each query record to one thread. Nobody has read the mmseqs source to confirm it. That tail is nail-3bf07b.

The logs are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-18-serial-overhead-48t/full-s12` and `replay-s12` on `catalyst`.
